title: RV & Boat Storage Fundamentals
description: Why vehicle owners need us and how big vehicles are at Greens, how to tell RV classes and boat types apart, open, covered and enclosed spaces at each Greens site, measuring so a vehicle fits the first time, the paperwork every vehicle needs, lot rules and risks, how vehicle and boat liens differ in California and Texas, and how to sell and keep vehicle tenants. Course 3 of the Greens Storage Academy.
overview: Why vehicle storage matters at Greens, with Greens' own numbers
RV classes and boat types, with real lengths and heights
Open, covered and enclosed spaces, and each Greens site's lot
Measuring for the right fit, with worked fit-checks
The paperwork every vehicle needs at move-in
Lot rules, risks and the site walk
Vehicle and boat liens in California and Texas, side by side
Selling, waitlists, upgrades and keeping vehicle tenants

questions.q: Which kind of towable RV is usually the tallest?
questions.explanation: Fifth wheels typically stand 12 to 13.5 ft, the tallest towable. Their raised front sits over a pickup bed, and the pin box overhang may not be in the brochure length.

questions.q: A motorhome has a truck cab with a sleeping bunk built out over the cab. What class is it?
questions.explanation: A Class C has a truck cab and an over-cab bunk. A Class A is bus-shaped, a Class B is a camper van, and a fifth wheel has no engine.

questions.q: A customer has a 23 ft wake boat. The maker lists it at 31 ft on its trailer with the tongue out. What length do you plan the space for?
questions.explanation: Storage length is the whole footprint on the trailer, tongue tip to the rearmost point. The 23 ft is hull length (LOA) only. Plan for 31 ft plus a margin of about 3 to 4 ft.

questions.q: A boat's advertised length (LOA) includes its outboard motor and its trailer.
questions.explanation: LOA runs bow to stern on the hull only. It leaves out the motor, swim platform, bow pulpit and trailer, which is why you measure tongue tip to the rearmost point.

questions.q: Which of these can make an RV taller than its brochure roof height? Choose all that apply.
options: A spare tire on the rear bumper
questions.explanation: Measure to the top of the tallest thing on the roof: air conditioners (about 10 to 14 in each), antennas, domes and solar panels. A rear spare adds length, not height.

questions.q: Without an oversize permit, about how wide is the body of an RV or boat on the road at most?
questions.explanation: The usual road width limit is 102 inches, or 8.5 ft, at the body. Mirrors, awnings and slide-outs stick out further, so plan for them.

questions.q: A Class A arrives towing a small car. How do you treat the car?
options: As part of the motorhome's space
As a separate vehicle that usually needs its own space or leaves with the owner
It can park in the aisle
It is not allowed on the lot
questions.explanation: A towed car (a toad) is a separate vehicle. It goes on the lease and in its own space, or it leaves with the owner.

questions.q: Which of these can change a boat's height on its trailer? Choose all that apply.
questions.explanation: Towers, biminis and T-tops raise height, and a bimini left up can push a pontoon over 13 ft. A swim platform adds length at the stern, not height.

questions.q: A travel trailer's box is 28 ft. The tongue adds 4 ft and a bike rack on the back adds 1 ft. What is its storage length before any margin?
questions.explanation: Measure coupler to the rearmost item: 28 + 4 + 1 = 33 ft. Then add the margin before you choose a space.

questions.q: Fairfield's spaces are 12x20, 12x22, 12x26, 12x32 and 12x48. A trailer measures 34 ft hitch to bumper. With a 3 ft margin, which is the smallest that fits?
questions.explanation: 34 + 3 = 37 ft. The 12x32 is shorter than the trailer itself, so the next size up, the 12x48, is the fit (sizes From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026).

questions.q: A fifth wheel measures 39 ft from the front of the pin box to the rear bumper. With a 3 ft margin, which is the smallest space that fits?
questions.explanation: 39 + 3 = 42 ft, so the 12x42 is the smallest that fits. A 12x40 would leave less than the margin.

questions.q: An operator rule of thumb says a 38 ft RV needs at least what length of space?
questions.explanation: Ladders, mirrors and bumpers add length, so a 38 ft RV needs at least a 42 ft space (Inside Self Storage, 2007). That is the 3 to 4 ft margin.

questions.q: An enclosed door is sold as 14 ft high. What should you assume about its clearance?
options: It may really be about 13 ft 8 in, so measure it
Height does not matter for doors
questions.explanation: A door sold as 14 ft may measure about 13 ft 8 in once hung, and a rain lip can cost another inch. Measure the real door and post the clear height.

questions.q: Temecula's covered sizes are 10x20, 11x30, 12x35, 12x40 and 12x50. A wake boat is 31 ft on its trailer. With a 3 ft margin, which is the smallest covered space that fits?
questions.explanation: 31 + 3 = 34 ft. The 11x30 is too short; the 12x35 is the smallest that fits, as long as the boat's height clears the posted clear height (sizes From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026).

questions.q: Put the start of the fit-check conversation in order.
options: What is the overall length, hitch to bumper?
For covered or enclosed: what is the height to the top?
Does it have slides, or does the tongue fold?
Offer the right size and record it in Cubby
questions.explanation: Type first, then length, then height, then what changes the footprint, then the offer. Writing it in Cubby saves the next person from asking again.

questions.q: For a covered or enclosed space, where do you measure a vehicle's height?
options: Ground to the highest point, such as the air conditioner, antenna or tower
Top of the tires to the roof
questions.explanation: Measure from the ground to the highest point with everything lowered: air conditioner shroud, antenna, tower, bimini, T-top or mast step.

questions.q: A tenant is backing a travel trailer into a drive-in space. Which way should it face when it is parked?
options: Tongue toward the dead end, so the back of the trailer is easy to reach
Tongue toward the aisle, so the tow vehicle backs to the coupler and pulls straight out next time
questions.explanation: A backed-in trailer leaves its coupler at the open end. Next time the truck backs a few feet to it and pulls straight out; nosed in, the owner hooks up in the corner and backs the whole rig out blind.

questions.q: What makes a pull-through space different from a drive-in space?
options: It is open at both ends, with an aisle at each, so the rig drives in one end and out the other
questions.explanation: A drive-in is open at one end only; a pull-through has an aisle at each end and nobody backs more than a truck length. It uses two aisle frontages, which is why it is the premium space.

lessons.title: Greens Vehicle Storage Rules
lessons.summary: What Greens collects for every vehicle, the house rules, the fees that apply to vehicles, and how a vehicle lien differs, with numbers from Greens' Cubby.

questions.q: About how many of Greens' 2,042 active leases store a vehicle?
questions.explanation: 759 of 2,042 active leases store a vehicle, more than one in three (From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026).

questions.q: Which Greens site is the biggest vehicle lot?
questions.explanation: Temecula has 481 parking spaces, the most at Greens, and the only covered spaces (From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026).

questions.q: A caller says their HOA sent a letter about their RV and asks what the rules are. What do you say?
options: Tell them HOAs cannot do that
Many cities and HOAs limit driveway parking; check with yours. Then help with the space.
Tell them they will be fined
questions.explanation: Staff never quote city code or HOA rules. Acknowledge, tell them to check with their HOA or city, then move to fit and paperwork.

questions.q: According to the 2025 RV Owner Demographic Profile (Go RVing and RVIA), how many U.S. households own an RV?
questions.explanation: 8.1 million households (2025). The 11.2 million figure is from a 2021 study with a different method, and RVIA says the two cannot be compared.

questions.q: A caller asks whether they can stay overnight in their RV on the lot. Where do you find Greens' answer?
options: Say yes if they are quiet
Greens Vehicle Storage Rules, or ask your manager
Make up a rule that sounds fair
questions.explanation: Living or sleeping in a stored vehicle is against common industry rules, but Greens' own rule lives on Greens Vehicle Storage Rules. Check it or ask your manager; never invent a house rule.

questions.q: What is a Class B?
options: A trailer that hitches in a pickup bed
questions.explanation: A Class B is a camper van on a van chassis, about 17 to 24 ft. High-roof vans run about 9.5 to 10 ft tall.

questions.q: How do you measure a fifth wheel's storage length?
options: Front of the nose or pin box to the rear bumper
questions.explanation: Measure from the front of the nose or pin box to the rear bumper and anything on it. The pin box overhang (3 to 5 ft) is often not in the brochure.

questions.q: A caller says, "It's a 28-foot travel trailer." What is your best follow-up?
options: "Is that the box or hitch to bumper, and is anything on the back?"
questions.explanation: The advertised length may or may not include the tongue, and racks or spares add more. Ask for hitch to bumper.

questions.q: A customer's 16 ft boat measured 22 ft on its trailer. What explains most of the difference?
questions.explanation: The trailer tongue alone added 6 ft. A boat's hull length leaves out the tongue, the motor and the swim platform.

questions.q: What does a swing (folding) trailer tongue do for storage?
options: Shortens the storage length by a few feet
questions.explanation: A folding tongue shortens the footprint. The Arc Sport example drops from 31 ft to 28 ft 2 in with the tongue folded.

questions.q: Which part of a trailerable sailboat often sticks out past the bow or stern while stored?
questions.explanation: The mast is laid down on the boat for towing and storage and can overhang the bow or stern. Measure to its end.

questions.q: Under a canopy, where is a covered space's clear height measured?
options: To the lowest point, usually the beam
To the top of the posts
questions.explanation: Clear height is to the lowest point under the roof, usually a beam. A rig too tall loses its air conditioner or antenna on it.

questions.q: Which Greens site has covered vehicle spaces?
questions.explanation: Temecula's 27 covered spaces are the only covered vehicle spaces at Greens (From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026).

questions.q: What is a pull-through space?
options: A space you drive into from one end and out of the other
questions.explanation: A pull-through lets a rig drive in one end and out the other with no backing. It is the easiest to use and sold at a premium.

questions.q: What kind of parking does Fairfield have?
questions.explanation: All 303 Fairfield spaces are open gravel, 12 ft wide, from 12x20 to 12x48 (From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026).

questions.q: How many pull-through spaces does Murrieta have?
questions.explanation: Murrieta has 36 pull-through spaces (18 at 12x33 and 18 at 12x50) on an all-paved lot of 161 (From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026).

questions.q: Which Greens site has the most parking spaces 40 ft and longer?
questions.explanation: Temecula has 147 spaces 40 ft and longer, more than any other Greens site (From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026).

questions.q: How many covered parking spaces does Escondido have?
questions.explanation: Every Escondido parking space is open: 80 gravel and 10 paved (From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026).

questions.q: What vehicle spaces does Valley Center have?
options: Three: two 12x38 enclosed garages and one open 11x35
questions.explanation: Valley Center has three vehicle spaces: two enclosed 12x38 garages, the only enclosed vehicle spaces at Greens, and one open 11x35 (From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026).

questions.q: About how much margin do you add to a vehicle's measured length?
questions.explanation: Add about 3 to 4 ft for walking room and a safety margin. Your manager may set a different margin for your site.

questions.q: A Class A is 36 ft bumper to bumper, plus a 1 ft ladder and a 2 ft bike rack. With a 3 ft margin, which space is the smallest that fits?
questions.explanation: 36 + 1 + 2 = 39 ft, plus 3 ft = 42 ft. A 12x40 is too short; the 12x45 is the smallest that fits.

questions.q: Where should the measured clear height be posted?
options: At every covered row and enclosed door, where the driver sees it before pulling in
questions.explanation: A posted clear height at every covered row and enclosed door prevents most roof damage and gives tenants a number to check every time.

questions.q: A customer stores a pontoon on its trailer. Which registrations do you need?
options: Both the boat's and the trailer's
questions.explanation: A boat and its trailer are registered separately. Collect current registration for both, in the tenant's name.

questions.q: The VIN on a customer's insurance card does not match the registration. What do you do?
options: Complete the move-in and fix it later
Stop: do not complete the move-in until it matches, and ask your manager
questions.explanation: The VIN or HIN must match on every document. A mismatch is a stop sign until it is resolved.

questions.q: Why do you record the title holder and lienholder at move-in?
options: Vehicle lien steps must reach them, and a lender's lien usually ranks ahead of the storage lien
questions.explanation: Both California and Texas vehicle lien steps require notice to the owners and lienholders on record. Getting the names at signing is far easier than later.

questions.q: Which photos belong in a vehicle move-in set? Choose all that apply.
options: All four sides of the vehicle
The plate and the VIN or HIN
The empty space and the vehicle in it
The inside of the tenant's cabinets
questions.explanation: Photos of all sides, damage, plate and VIN or HIN, and the space are the baseline for any later dispute. You never search inside a tenant's vehicle.

questions.q: At a Texas site, what must exist for TPWD's lien foreclosure process to work on a boat?
options: A written, signed rental agreement containing the self-service storage lien
questions.explanation: TPWD form PWD 309B requires a written, signed rental agreement containing the lien. Never let a vehicle in at a Texas site before the lease is signed.

questions.q: A tenant asks who pays if their RV is damaged on the lot. What is true?
questions.explanation: The tenant's own insurance covers their vehicle. Greens' insurance does not, and protection plans usually exclude vehicles; only one Greens vehicle lease is on a plan (From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026).

questions.q: What is Greens' Vehicle Lien Fee in California?
questions.explanation: The Vehicle Lien Fee is $350.00, applied with the 61st day vehicle task (From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026).

questions.q: What is the Administration Fee on a Greens vehicle move-in in California?
questions.explanation: The Administration Fee is $25.00 at all five sites (From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026). The $10.00 fee is the mailbox one.

questions.q: Why is washing a vehicle in its space not allowed?
options: Soap, oil and grime run into storm drains
questions.explanation: Wash water carries soap, oil and grime into storm drains. Washing belongs only in a wash bay, where a site has one.

questions.q: What is the common propane rule for a stored RV?
options: Valves closed at the source whenever stored
questions.explanation: Propane valves are closed at the source whenever the RV is stored; some facilities require tanks disconnected or empty.

questions.q: On a walk you smell gas near a motorhome. What do you do first?
questions.explanation: Gas, smoke or fuel: leave the area and call 911 first, then tell your manager. Never handle a tenant's propane yourself.

questions.q: Which is an early warning sign that a vehicle may be abandoned?
questions.explanation: Expired tags, flat tires, a cover gone and no visits are early signs of abandonment. Note expired tags on every walk.

questions.q: You find a car with no lease parked in an empty space. What do you do?
options: Photograph it, check Cubby and tell your manager
questions.explanation: A vehicle with no lease is not a lien case. Photograph it, check Cubby, and tell your manager. Never tow, boot or move it yourself.

questions.q: What does every exception on a lot walk need?
options: A verbal mention to a coworker
A dated photo and a note
questions.explanation: A dated photo and a note: in Cubby for a tenant's vehicle or account, in Nexus for the site. A problem with no photo did not happen in a later dispute.

questions.q: The gate is closing on long rigs before they clear. Where do you report it?
options: In Nexus: Report a Problem at the site's QR tag, or a ticket
questions.explanation: Site problems go to Nexus: Report a Problem or a ticket, with a photo. Tenant and account issues go on the lease in Cubby.

questions.q: Put the damage incident steps in order.
options: Make sure everyone is safe; call 911 if needed
Write the incident report the same day
questions.explanation: Safety first, then photos, then names and insurance, then the report the same day and your manager, who decides about the insurer. Never admit fault.

questions.q: A tenant backs into a bollard and asks, "You'll cover this, right?" What do you say?
options: "I'm documenting everything and passing it to my manager."
questions.explanation: Never admit fault or promise payment. Document it, report it the same day and pass it to your manager.

questions.q: Hail hits a Texas site in the afternoon. What do you do?
options: Walk the lot, photograph damage, and report to your manager without saying who is responsible
questions.explanation: Walk after every weather event, photograph damage to vehicles and the canopy, and report it. Do not admit fault.

questions.q: In California, under Bus. & Prof. Code 21702.5, how is a storage lien on a registered vehicle enforced?
options: Under Civil Code 3071, the DMV lien sale process
questions.explanation: 21702.5 sends vehicles to Civil Code 3071 (the DMV lien sale) and vessels to Harbors and Navigation Code 503, never the unit sale steps. Training only, not legal advice.

questions.q: In California, which law governs the lien sale of a vessel stored at a self-storage facility?
questions.explanation: Vessels go through the Boaters Lien Law, Harbors and Navigation Code 503, with DMV authorization for a vessel worth more than $1,500. Training only, not legal advice.

questions.q: For a vehicle stored at a self-storage facility in California, the DMV's short process for vehicles worth $4,000 or less (Civil Code 3072) can be used.
questions.explanation: California DMV says a vehicle at a self-service storage facility is sold under Civil Code 3071 whatever its value; the 3072 short process cannot be used. Training only, not legal advice.

questions.q: Under 21702.5, a California storage lien on a vehicle may not include charges accruing more than how long after it attaches?
questions.explanation: The lien may not include rent or other charges accruing more than 60 days after it attaches. Training only, not legal advice.

questions.q: Under 21702.5, when may a California facility owner have a defaulted vehicle towed instead of holding a lien sale?
options: Any time after the 1st late day
Once rent is 60 days unpaid, the preliminary lien notice was sent, and at least 10 days' mailed notice names the tow company
questions.explanation: Rent 60 days unpaid, the preliminary notice sent, and at least 10 days' notice by first-class mail with a certificate of mailing naming the tow company. Your manager decides, never you.

questions.q: Under Texas Property Code 59.0445, by when must a facility notify the owner and every recorded lienholder of a titled vehicle or boat?
options: Never; only the tenant is notified
questions.explanation: Within 30 days after taking possession, with the charges and that it may be sold if not paid before the 31st day. Training only, not legal advice.

questions.q: Under the Texas towing option (SB 1181, since 09/01/2021), which must ALL be true before a defaulted vehicle is towed? Choose all that apply.
options: The written rental agreement expressly authorizes towing
The tenant did not pay by the 14th day after the lien notice was delivered
A licensed vehicle storage facility agrees in writing to accept it
A court has ordered the tow
questions.explanation: All three are required: towing authorized in the lease, no payment by the 14th day after notice, and a VSF's written agreement. No court order is needed. Training only, not legal advice.

questions.q: In Texas, what happens to the storage lien once a defaulted vehicle is towed to a vehicle storage facility under the towing option?
options: It ends, so the unpaid rent is not recovered from the vehicle
It moves to the tow company
questions.explanation: Under Property Code 59.053, the storage lien is extinguished once the vehicle is towed. Training only, not legal advice.

questions.q: What Cubby task does a Greens vehicle account reach on day 61 of delinquency?
questions.explanation: Day 61 raises "61st - Vehicle Lien Filing/Tow Notice" with a $350.00 Vehicle Lien Fee (From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026). It goes to your manager.

questions.q: A coworker suggests adding a defaulted car to next week's unit auction. What is right?
options: A titled vehicle never goes to the unit auction; tell your manager
questions.explanation: Titled vehicles and boats follow the state vehicle or vessel lien process, never the unit auction. Training only, not legal advice. When in doubt, stop and ask your manager.

questions.q: A caller asks the monthly price of a 12x32 space at Fairfield. Where do you get the rate you quote?
options: From Cubby's current rate for that space
questions.explanation: Rates change. The Site Profile and lesson figures are a snapshot from 11/2026; always quote today's rate from Cubby.

questions.q: A caller asks, "Is it secure?" What is the best answer?
options: Describe what is real: the gate code, cameras where the site has them, lighting and lot walks; insurance is still required
questions.explanation: Describe real security measures and never promise nothing will happen. The tenant's own insurance is still required.

questions.q: A caller says the place down the road is cheaper. What do you do?
options: Ask what they get there (aisles, hours, surface, amenities) and show what Greens offers, never criticizing the competitor
questions.explanation: Compare what they get, not just the price, and never disparage a competitor.

questions.q: A customer asks whether their 13 ft 6 in fifth wheel fits under your covered spaces. What do you do?
options: Never guess: check the posted clear height, and offer open space now if it is not clearly enough
questions.explanation: Never guess a height. Check the measured, posted clear height; if it is not clearly enough, offer an open space now and the waitlist.

questions.q: A customer wants covered space and none is open. What path keeps the customer?
options: Tell them to call back in six months
Rent an open space that fits now, add them to the covered waitlist, and upgrade them when one opens
Put them under a canopy in the aisle
questions.explanation: Open now, covered later keeps the customer on the lot and raises revenue at the upgrade. Re-check the fit when you upgrade.

questions.q: Which details belong in a vehicle waitlist entry so you can make an offer that fits? Choose all that apply.
options: The product wanted (covered, enclosed, pull-through, size)
questions.explanation: Capture the fit details with the contact: type, length, height, product and acceptable sites, so you can say "I have your space" without a second fit-check.

questions.q: A tenant plans to cancel for the winter and come back in spring. What do you tell them?
options: Their space is held for free
The rental is month to month, so they may leave, but the space may not be there when they return; offer the waitlist
They must pay a fee to leave
questions.explanation: Be honest: the space may be gone, especially a long, covered or pull-through one. Offer to note their return date for the waitlist.

questions.q: What is a toad?
options: A car towed behind a motorhome
questions.explanation: A toad (or dinghy) is a car towed behind a motorhome. It is a separate vehicle and usually needs its own space.

questions.q: On a California title, who is the legal owner when there is a loan?
questions.explanation: The legal owner is the lender; the registered owner is the person who uses it. Both must be reached in the vehicle lien process.

questions.q: Why do staff never move a tenant's vehicle?
options: Handling it means taking on care, custody and control, with liability and insurance Greens would need
questions.explanation: An operator who parks or moves vehicles takes on care, custody and control of them and needs matching insurance. The tenant moves it, or your manager decides.

questions.q: Cubby names a pricing group "12' x 32' Parking - Gravel, Drive-In." What does Drive-In tell you about the space?
options: It is open at one end only; a vehicle goes in and comes out the same way
questions.explanation: Drive-in is the ordinary one-end space, the same shape the Site Profile pages call back-in (drive-in).

questions.q: A Class A motorhome is backed into a drive-in space until its rear tires touch the wheel stop. A chain-link fence stands 3 ft behind the stop. What is the risk?
options: None; the wheel stop is the end of the space
The rear overhang behind the wheels can be 8 to 12 ft and may hit the fence
The front will stick into the aisle
questions.explanation: A wheel stop marks where the tires stop, not where the vehicle ends. The body behind the rear wheels hangs past it.

questions.q: A tenant enters an angled row against its arrow. What happens?
options: Nothing; angled spaces work from either direction
Every space becomes a jackknife turn instead of a gentle curve
The gate will not let him out
The spaces are too narrow from that side
questions.explanation: Angled spaces are built for one direction of travel. From the wrong one the turn is a sharp reverse. Faded arrows on an angled row are a same-day report.

questions.q: Why are pull-through spaces scarce and priced above other spaces?
options: Each one uses two aisle frontages, so a lot gives up spaces to make one, and the no-backing convenience is what big-rig owners pay for
They are longer than every other space
Cubby limits how many a site can have
questions.explanation: A pull-through needs an aisle at each end. Murrieta's run $249 to $279 against its typical $184 (From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026).
